source.title: "World Knowledge" in the Weights: Reading Concept Circuits of Vision Transformers
source.authors: Yan-Lin Chen; Li Tang; Peng Xi

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates CLT-based concept circuits in vision transformers, but does not measure neuron poles or test any of the listed claims about neuron interpretability or neuron-based circuits.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemantic neurons and sparse features as background, but its own units are learned CLT concepts, not neurons or neuron poles. Its circuit-ablation and faithfulness results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; they do not establish how interpretable neurons are. Figure 5 reports curves without numeric values; the text gives only the stated CLIP average comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study trains cross-layer transcoders on vision transformers and evaluates CLT-learned concept circuits (ablation accuracy, faithfulness/completeness vs SAEs, spurious-correlation steering). It never measures how interpretable individual neurons or neuron poles are, never builds circuits from the model's own neurons, and does not score neuron explanations. Polysemantic neurons appear only as background motivation. It neither tests nor uses the claim's versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Add that the authors also report CLT circuits enable automatic spurious-correlation discovery and removal (worst-group Waterbirds accuracy +23 points, 11.0% over prior methods), and model comparison across CLIP, DINO and ViT. Limitations stated: CLTs mainly capture MLP paths, interpretation needs human inspection, global graphs not fully causal.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains cross-layer transcoders to form sparse concept features and circuits in vision transformers; it does not use or replicate a neuron-pole audit.
record.method_sensitivity: CLT training hyperparameters affect explained variance and monosemanticity: the paper reports that increasing L0 sparsity and dictionary size raises explained variance but lowers monosemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablating top-10 concepts from global CLT circuits lowers ImageNet accuracy (CLIP 0.60 to 0.22, ViT 0.70 to 0.44, DINO 0.76 to 0.62), while random ablation changes it little.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global CLT concept circuits read from weights identify causally important concepts in vision transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: CLT-based instance circuits beat matched SAE circuits on faithfulness and completeness; on CLIP by 24.4% and 22.1% on average.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision transformers, transcoder-based replacement circuits are more faithful than SAE-based circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher L0 and dictionary size raise CLT explained variance but lower feature monosemanticity (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For learned dictionaries on ViTs, reconstruction and feature monosemanticity trade off.

record.problems: The reported experiments concern CLT-learned concepts in vision transformers, not neuron poles. The faithfulness curves in Fig. 5 do not have numeric values stated in the text except for the CLIP average comparisons. The paper notes that CLTs primarily capture MLP pathways, only indirectly reflect attention structure, require human inspection for concept interpretation, and that global graphs do not fully capture causal relations.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted under the row cap. Figure 5's plotted values for DINO, ViT, and other node counts were not transcribed because they are not numerically stated in the text.

untested.parts: Neuron interpretability shares across language models, dense and MoE, at scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization.
Share of interpretable neurons as a function of architecture, regularization and tools; the study measures monosemanticity only for CLT features, not neurons.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model; the study uses a trained CLT replacement and does not compare to neuron graphs.
Whether activating-example explanations of neurons predict firing.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

missing.what: Waterbirds steering result: worst-group accuracy 0.48 to 0.71 with CLT ablation vs 0.53 SAE, 0.60 SpLiCE (Table 2). Not bearing on any version, but unrecorded and undeclared.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Reader's T6/discusses judgment is right. All rows correctly linked to none. The CLT 'monosemanticity' metric is about learned features, not neurons, so it cannot speak to V4 neuron shares.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole job counts and the shares with one, two, or unknown jobs.
Neuron interpretability shares across model families, architectures, or scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, and recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability rates in vision models and the proposed architecture, regularization, and tool explanations.
Whether attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict where neurons fire on new examples.
Automated scores for neuron explanations simulated on new text.
